name: Algebra 1 Language / Reading / Tone Profile
benchmark_source: Conceptual Physics textbook/curriculum sections supplied by teacher
target_reader: High-school Algebra 1; accessible, mature, conceptually explanatory, and mathematically precise.
readability: Benchmark Conceptual Physics in feel: clear high-school prose, concrete examples, correct vocabulary, and enough explanation for independent rereading; do not chase a numeric readability score.

notes_reading.benchmark: Conceptual Physics supplied by the teacher: direct conceptual textbook voice that explains relationships and reasoning with concrete examples.
notes_reading.default_paragraphs_per_substantial_readi: usually 3-4 developed paragraphs; a little more is better when useful
notes_reading.sentences_per_paragraph: usually 3-5 natural sentences; vary with the idea
notes_reading.rule: Do not produce thin blurbs or dry procedure lists merely to reach the next problem. Each paragraph advances meaning, representation, reasoning, or why the mathematics works.
notes_reading.vocabulary: Bold a target vocabulary/notation term at its first meaningful introduction/definition in the reading; later recurrence normally returns to regular weight.

bank_language: Vary generic/narrative wording when useful; repeated concise procedural Practice stems are allowed.
Use realistic contexts only when they serve the mathematics.
Do not unnecessarily state a computed quantity as a given.
Use correct notation and vocabulary at the level supported by the Assessment Plan.
avoid: college-level abstraction when simpler precise prose works
repetitive generic pseudocontext/narrative skeletons outside purposeful procedural practice
thin one- or two-paragraph instructional blurbs
procedure-only reading with no conceptual explanation

bank_item_language_contract.context_rule: Use a context only when the quantities/decision/interpretation matter. Name real quantities and natural units; otherwise state the mathematics directly.
bank_item_language_contract.sentence_structure: Do not create fake variety by swapping only nouns/numbers in generic contexts. This does not prohibit repeated direct procedural Practice stems or numeric variants.
bank_item_language_contract.grammar: Audit article agreement, subject-verb agreement, and singular/plural agreement, especially after template substitution.
bank_item_language_contract.benchmark: Student prompts should sound like native Algebra 1 course material calibrated by the embedded Algebra/CPM corpus, not generator prose.
